summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, and Jena, and under teachers including Engel, Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy, later holding a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin.
Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1993-1997), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, and held posts at McGill (1960-1964), Yale (1966-1971), and the University of Toronto and Trinity College (1971-1999).

Willard Van Orman Quine worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University, where he served as Junior Fellow (1933-1936), Assistant Professor (1940), and Edgar Pierce Chair of Philosophy (1948-1978).

Willem Bollée was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1947-1956) and the University of Hamburg (habilitated by 1975). He held posts at the University of Münster (1971-1978) and Heidelberg University (~1972-1992).

Willem Caland was an Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Hendrik Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held positions as lecturer of Indology (1903) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906-1929) at Utrecht University, and at Leiden (1913-1914).
Willem van der Molen worked in linguistics and Sinology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971-1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1983-2017) and the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Virginia (attested 1992), Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and Chung-Hwa Institute (attested 2008).
William Blackstone was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford (~1738-1745), and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1758-1766).

William C. Kirby works in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth and at Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn, later holding posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1979-1992), Harvard University (1992), and the Fairbank Center (~2006-2013).
William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma and Ramram Basu (~1793-1801). In 1801, he held a post as Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College.

William Dwight Whitney worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, and Roth, he held posts at Yale University as Professor of Sanskrit (1853, 1869-1894) and the American Oriental Society.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics as a visiting professor.

William Edward Soothill worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University (1911) and Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford (1920).

William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1787-1792).
William Evans Hoyle was a scholar who completed his studies at Christ Church, University of Oxford (~1874-1877) and the University of Manchester.
William F. Powell is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held a career at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 1986, 2026).
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and held a post with the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Bonn under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He held posts at Indiana University (~1972-1973) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1983).

William Henry Denham Rouse worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge, held a fellowship at Christ's College (1888), and taught at Bedford School, Cheltenham College, Rugby School (~1895-1901), and The Perse School (1902-1928).
